nodes.summary: `i` and `j` are adjacent in the skeleton of the graph.
nodes.title: Adjacency in the skeleton of a Bayesian network

nodes.summary: The back-door adjustment (Pearl 1995; Pearl 2009, Theorem 3.3.2): if the set `Z` contains no descendant of the treatment node `k` and blocks every path between `k` and the outcome node `y` that begins with an arrow into `k`, then `P(X_y = v | do(X_k = a)) = ∑_z P(Z = z) P(X_y = v | X_k = a, Z = z)`, assuming `P(X_k = a, Z = z) > 0` whenever `P(Z = z) > 0`.
nodes.title: The back-door adjustment

nodes.summary: Blocking at a node does not depend on the direction in which the path is read.
nodes.title: Blocking at a node is independent of path direction

nodes.summary: The consecutive nodes `u, m, w` of a path are blocked by `Z` (Pearl 2009, Definition 1.2.3): either `m` is a collider `u → m ← w` none of whose descendants is in `Z`, or `m` is not a collider (a chain or a fork) and `m ∈ Z`.
nodes.title: Blocking at a node of a path

nodes.summary: d-separation (Pearl 1988; Pearl 2009, Definition 1.2.3): `Z` d-separates `X` from `Y` if every path between a node of `X` and a node of `Y` is blocked by `Z`.
nodes.title: d-separation

nodes.summary: The arrows of `b.mutilateSet W w` are those of `b` not pointing into `W`.
nodes.title: Arrows of the mutilated network

nodes.summary: The edge `i → j` of the network's graph: `i` is a parent of `j`.
nodes.title: Edge of a Bayesian network

nodes.summary: After removing the arrows into `W`, a node of `W` is a descendant only of itself.
nodes.title: Intervened nodes descend only from themselves

nodes.summary: The front-door adjustment (Pearl 1995; Pearl 2009, Theorem 3.3.4): if the set `M` intercepts every directed path from the treatment node `k` to the outcome node `y`, no path from `k` to a node of `M` that begins with an arrow into `k` is open (blocked by `∅`), and every path from a node of `M` to `y` that begins with an arrow into that node is blocked by `{k}`, then…
nodes.title: The front-door adjustment

nodes.summary: The parents of every other node are unchanged by the intervention.
nodes.title: Intervention leaves the parents of other nodes unchanged

nodes.summary: The parents of the intervened node are deleted.
nodes.title: Intervention deletes the parents of the intervened node

nodes.summary: The mechanism of node `k` is replaced by the point mass at `a`, and all incoming arrows to `k` are deleted (its parent set becomes `∅`); every other node keeps its parents and its table. (The new table of `k` is the point mass on the empty parent set; the tables of the other nodes are transported along the equality of their parent sets.)
nodes.title: The intervention `do(X_k = a)`

nodes.summary: `j` is a descendant of `i` (every node is its own descendant).
nodes.title: Descendant relation in a Bayesian network

nodes.summary: The reverse of a path from `x` to `y` is a path from `y` to `x`.
nodes.title: The reverse of a path is a path

nodes.summary: A path of the skeleton from `x` to `y`: a list of distinct nodes, consecutive ones adjacent, starting at `x` and ending at `y`.
nodes.title: Path in the skeleton of a Bayesian network

nodes.summary: For `x k = a`, `P(x) = P(x | do(X_k = a)) · p_k(a | x_{pa k})`.
nodes.title: Joint law as interventional law times the node's table

nodes.summary: After `do(X_k = a)`, assignments with `x k ≠ a` have probability `0`.
nodes.title: Assignments contradicting an intervention have probability zero

nodes.summary: The truncated factorization (Pearl 2009, eq. (3.10)): after `do(X_k = a)` the joint is the product of the tables of all nodes other than `k` on assignments with `x_k = a`, and `0` elsewhere.
nodes.title: The truncated factorization

nodes.summary: After `do(X_W = w)`, the joint is the product of the tables of the nodes outside `W` on assignments agreeing with `w` on `W`.
nodes.title: The truncated factorization for a set of nodes

nodes.summary: The intervention `do(X_k = a)` does not change the law of the non-descendants of `k`.
nodes.title: The intervention `do(X_k = a)` does not change the law of the non-descendants of `k`

nodes.summary: The network of the intervention `do(X_W = w)` with the arrows into `W` removed: every node `j ∈ W` has no parents and the point mass at `w j` as its table.
nodes.title: Mutilated network of a set intervention

nodes.summary: A descendant after removing the arrows into `W` is a descendant in `b`.
nodes.title: Descendants in the mutilated network are descendants in the original

nodes.summary: The values of the parents of node `k` in a full assignment `x`.
nodes.title: Parent values of a node

nodes.summary: If a path is blocked by `Z`, so is its reverse.
nodes.title: Reversal preserves blocked paths

nodes.summary: A path is blocked by `Z` if some three consecutive nodes of it are.
nodes.title: Blocked path

nodes.summary: The table of node `k` is the conditional law of `X_k` given its parents: `P(X_k = a, pa_k = z) = p_k (a | z) P(pa_k = z)`.
nodes.title: A node's table is its conditional law given its parents

nodes.summary: For a set `Z` of predecessors of `k` containing its parents, the table of `k` is its conditional law given `Z`: `P(X_k = a, Z = z) = p_k (a | z_{pa k}) P(Z = z)`.
nodes.title: A node's table is its conditional law given a predecessor set

nodes.summary: Adjustment for the direct causes when the table of node `k` gives the value `a` positive probability at every value of the parents.
nodes.title: Adjustment for the direct causes under table positivity

nodes.summary: Back-door adjustment for a set of predecessors containing the parents, when the table of node `k` gives the value `a` positive probability at every value of the parents.
nodes.title: Back-door adjustment for a set of predecessors

nodes.summary: Let `Z` be a set of nodes preceding `k` in the topological order (so `Z` contains no descendant of `k`) that contains the parents of `k`. Then `Z` meets the back-door criterion for every outcome node `y ∉ Z` (a path from `k` to `y` that starts with an arrow into `k` starts `k ← p` with `p ∈ pa(k) ⊆ Z`, an interior non-collider, so it is blocked), and for every function `f` of the variables…
nodes.title: Back-door adjustment for a set of predecessors containing the parents

nodes.summary: Adjustment for the direct causes (Pearl 2009, Theorem 3.2.2; the case `Z = pa(X)` of the back-door adjustment): for every function `f` of the variables, `E[f | do(X_k = a)] = ∑_z P(pa_k = z) E[f | X_k = a, pa_k = z]`, assuming `P(X_k = a, pa_k = z) > 0` whenever `P(pa_k = z) > 0`.
nodes.title: Adjustment for the direct causes

nodes.summary: The intervention `do(X_k = a)` does not change the law of the parents of node `k`.
nodes.title: Intervention preserves the law of the parents

nodes.summary: Symmetry of d-separation. d-separation is symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of d-separation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
